source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains substantial assurance and evidentiary conviction without reducing faith to optimism.
key_decisions.before: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
key_decisions.after: Now faith is the assurance of what is hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves creation by speech and visible/invisible contrast.
key_decisions.before: By faith we understand that the ages were prepared by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible.
key_decisions.after: By faith we understand that the ages were formed by God's word, so that what is seen did not come from visible things.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith we understand that the ages were prepared by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps both names, comparative offering and postmortem voice.
key_decisions.before: By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain. Through it he received commendation as righteous, God himself bearing witness by accepting his gifts; and through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.
key_decisions.after: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. Through it he was approved as righteous, God testifying about his gifts; and through faith, though dead, he still speaks.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain. Through it he received commendation as righteous, God himself bearing witness by accepting his gifts; and through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains repeated translation/taking language and divine pleasure.
key_decisions.before: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken he received commendation as one who had pleased God.
key_decisions.after: By faith Enoch was taken away so that he did not see death, and he could not be found because God had taken him. Before he was taken, he was approved as pleasing to God.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken he received commendation as one who had pleased God.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves warning, household rescue, world judgment and inheritance.
key_decisions.before: By faith Noah, having been warned by God about events as yet unseen, in reverent fear constructed an ark for the saving of his household. Through this faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by trust.
key_decisions.after: By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen, responded with reverence and built an ark to save his household. By this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Noah, having been warned by God about events as yet unseen, in reverent fear constructed an ark for the saving of his household. Through this faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps call, obedience, inheritance and ignorance.
key_decisions.before: By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed and went out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
key_decisions.after: By faith Abraham obeyed when called to leave for a place he was to receive as an inheritance. He left without knowing where he was going.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed and went out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves alien residence, tents and named coheirs.
key_decisions.before: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
key_decisions.after: By faith he lived as a foreigner in the promised land as in a land belonging to others, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.

key_decisions.rationale: Follows the pinned Sarah-as-subject reading and retains bodily impossibility.
key_decisions.before: By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive seed, even when she was past the proper age, since she considered him faithful who had promised.
key_decisions.after: By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive, even past the proper age, because she considered the one who promised faithful.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive seed, even when she was past the proper age, since she considered him faithful who had promised.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps near-death, both vast-number similes and descent.
key_decisions.before: So from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as the innumerable grains of sand by the seashore.
key_decisions.after: Therefore, from one man—and one already as good as dead—came descendants as numerous as the stars in heaven and as countless as the sand along the seashore.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as the innumerable grains of sand by the seashore.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves death before fulfillment and alien identity.
key_decisions.before: All these died in faith, not having received what was promised, but having seen and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
key_decisions.after: All these died in faith without receiving the promises. They saw and welcomed them from far away and confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: All these died in faith, not having received what was promised, but having seen and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps better/heavenly identification and divine city preparation.
key_decisions.before: But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.
key_decisions.after: But now they desire a better land—a heavenly one. Therefore, God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the attempted child sacrifice, both names and promise tension.
key_decisions.before: By faith Abraham, when he was being tested, offered up Isaac, and the one who had received the promises was offering up his only son,
key_decisions.after: By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac. The one who had received the promises was offering his one and only son,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Abraham, when he was being tested, offered up Isaac, and the one who had received the promises was offering up his only son,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps named son and lineage quotation.
key_decisions.before: of whom it was said, “Through Isaac will your descendants be called.”
key_decisions.after: about whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your offspring will be named.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of whom it was said, “Through Isaac shall your descendants be called.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves resurrection reasoning and parable-like return.
key_decisions.before: He reasoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead—and figuratively he did receive him back.
key_decisions.after: Abraham reasoned that God was able even to raise someone from the dead, and in a figurative sense he did receive Isaac back.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: He reasoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead—and figuratively he did receive him back.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains death setting, both grandsons collectively and staff.
key_decisions.before: By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the head of his staff.
key_decisions.after: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped while leaning on the top of his staff.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the head of his staff.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps exodus anticipation and burial remains.
key_decisions.before: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave directions concerning his bones.
key_decisions.after: By faith Joseph, near the end of his life, mentioned the exodus of Israel's children and gave instructions about his bones.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave directions concerning his bones.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves exact duration, both parents and royal threat.
key_decisions.before: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king’s edict.
key_decisions.after: By faith Moses, after he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king's decree.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king’s edict.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps identity refusal and named royal relation.
key_decisions.before: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,
key_decisions.after: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh's daughter.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

key_decisions.rationale: Retains chosen affliction and brief pleasure.
key_decisions.before: choosing rather to suffer ill-treatment with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.
key_decisions.after: He chose to suffer mistreatment with God's people rather than enjoy sin's temporary pleasure.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: choosing rather to suffer ill-treatment with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps surprising Christ reference and economic comparison.
key_decisions.before: He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.
key_decisions.after: He considered disgrace for the Christ greater wealth than Egypt's treasures, because he was looking toward the reward.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves departure, royal rage and paradoxical sight.
key_decisions.before: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible.
key_decisions.after: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king's anger, for he persevered as though seeing the invisible one.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps named feast, blood and lethal threat.
key_decisions.before: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.
key_decisions.after: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains named sea, miracle and drowning.
key_decisions.before: By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do the same, were swallowed up.
key_decisions.after: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; when the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do the same, were swallowed up.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps place, walls and exact duration.
key_decisions.before: By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been encircled for seven days.
key_decisions.after: By faith Jericho's walls fell after being encircled for seven days.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been encircled for seven days.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps name, stigmatized occupation and protective reception.
key_decisions.before: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with people who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.
key_decisions.after: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves all six names and rhetorical compression.
key_decisions.before: And what more will I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,
key_decisions.after: And what more should I say? Time would fail me if I told about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps women as agents/recipients, torture and chosen nonrelease.
key_decisions.before: Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might rise to a better life.
key_decisions.after: Women received their dead back by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might rise to a better life.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves all public and custodial abuse.
key_decisions.before: Still others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
key_decisions.after: Others experienced mockery and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Still others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps graphic killings, clothing and three forms of deprivation.
key_decisions.before: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—
key_decisions.after: They were stoned, sawn in two and killed by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted and mistreated—
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—

key_decisions.rationale: Retains evaluative reversal and every refuge.
key_decisions.before: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering over deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
key_decisions.after: the world was not worthy of them—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves and holes in the ground.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering over deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves intergenerational completion and inclusion.
key_decisions.before: since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made complete.
key_decisions.after: because God had provided something better for us, so that they would not be perfected without us.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made complete.
